template_name: Natural Material Stress Reduction via Multi-Modal Convergence
calibration_constraint: VISUAL-I T1 owns visual fractal channel; MULTI-I owns convergence bonus only

mechanism_chain.process: Natural materials (wood, natural stone, natural fibre) emit multi-sensory signals: visual texture with fractal statistics (T1 channel, owned by VISUAL-I), haptic warmth and moderate roughness (CT pathway), and olfactory volatile organic compounds (phytoncides from wood).
mechanism_chain.substrate: Parallel sensory pathways: visual (PPA → ventral stream), haptic (CT → insular cortex), olfactory (olfactory bulb → piriform → amygdala)
mechanism_chain.source: Li et al. (2009); McGlone et al. (2014); Taylor et al. (2005)

data: Natural materials (wood, stone, natural fibre) emit multi-sensory signals
Visual: fractal statistics (owned by VISUAL-I T1)
Haptic: warmth (low λ) + moderate roughness (optimal Ra) = CT pathway activation
Olfactory: phytoncides from wood (20-80 μg/m³ indoor concentrations)
justification.backing: Li et al. (2009) phytoncide measurements. McGlone et al. (2014) haptic properties. Taylor et al. (2005) on visual fractal statistics of nature. Li (2010) on forest therapy research.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.6 reflects direct measurement of natural material signals. MECHANISM warrant: natural material properties are documented in materials science and physiology.
justification.rebuttal: Phytoncide indoor concentrations are variable (depends on ventilation, material finish). Haptic properties vary with moisture and temperature.
competing_accounts: Natural materials are not inherently different from synthetic: refuted by distinct phytoncide presence and haptic profiles
Visual properties alone account for natural material effects: refuted by stress reduction in blind individuals exposed to natural materials
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Li phytoncide authority, McGlone haptic authority

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.process: Each channel independently activates parasympathetic pathways: visual fractal statistics → perceptual fluency → reduced cortical arousal; haptic warmth/roughness → CT → insular → parasympathetic shift; phytoncides → olfactory → limbic → HPA axis suppression.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Three independent parasympathetic activation pathways converging on autonomic regulation

data: Visual fractal statistics → perceptual fluency → reduced cortical arousal (see VISUAL-I T1 for mechanism)
Haptic warmth/roughness → CT afferent firing → posterior insula → parasympathetic shift (see CT_AFFECTIVE_TOUCH_001)
Phytoncides → olfactory receptors → olfactory bulb → amygdala → HPA axis suppression (Li et al., 2009)
Three independent pathways converging on parasympathetic activation
justification.backing: Li (2010) review of phytoncide pathways. Morrison (2016) on CT insular pathway. Multiple independent literatures (visual perceptual fluency, olfactory stress reduction, autonomic regulation).
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.55 reflects convergent evidence from independent domains. EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE warrant: each pathway is established; convergence is inferred.
justification.rebuttal: Pathways may not be truly independent at higher levels (OFC, mPFC). Top-down expectations could amplify or suppress individual channel effects.
competing_accounts: Single dominant pathway explains natural material effects: refuted by effects persisting when one channel is removed
Pathways are competitive, not convergent: refuted by additive/synergistic stress reduction effects
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Li (phytoncide), Morrison (haptic), independent experts

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: Nature view exposure and restoration outcomes show consistent covariance across environmental psychology and neuroscience studies; strong effect sizes and biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.process: Convergent parasympathetic activation from independent pathways produces a convergence bonus: the combined stress reduction exceeds the sum of individual channel effects by approximately 20% (field data from Heerwagen).
mechanism_chain.substrate: Convergent autonomic regulation: multiple independent inputs → parasympathetic dominance

data: Combined stress reduction exceeds arithmetic sum of individual channel effects
Mechanism: convergent parasympathetic activation from independent pathways
justification.backing: Heerwagen & Hase (2001) field observations. Heerwagen (2009) post-occupancy data. Autonomic physiology literature on convergent parasympathetic inputs.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.45 reflects field data but limited controlled studies. CAPACITY warrant: convergence bonus is measured in field; mechanism is partially inferred.
justification.rebuttal: Field confounds (occupant expectations, context effects) may inflate convergence bonus. Individual variability in autonomic response is substantial.
competing_accounts: Multi-channel exposure is no better than single best channel: refuted by measured convergence bonus
Channels are strictly additive: refuted by synergistic effects exceeding sum
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Heerwagen field authority

mechanism_chain.process: Outcome: measurable stress reduction (cortisol ↓ ~8–15%, blood pressure ↓, HRV shift toward parasympathetic, NK cell activity ↑ ~50%). Duration of effect: hours for physiological markers; accumulated benefit from chronic exposure.

data: Stress reduction: cortisol ↓ ~8-15%, blood pressure ↓, HRV shift to parasympathetic
Duration: hours for physiological markers; accumulated benefit from chronic exposure
justification.backing: Li et al. (2009) forest therapy studies with cortisol and NK cell data. Li (2010) literature review. Multiple independent studies on nature exposure and stress reduction.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.5 reflects convergent physiological measurements. EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE warrant: physiological outcomes are directly measured.
justification.rebuttal: Effect sizes vary widely across studies. Individual differences in stress response are substantial. Habituation to natural environments may occur.
competing_accounts: Stress reduction is purely psychological (placebo): refuted by stress reduction in sleep, non-conscious contexts
Nature exposure is not superior to other stress-reduction methods: partially true; comparisons show moderate effects
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Li forest therapy authority

visual_channel_effect.interpretation: Visual fractal statistics stress reduction is calibrated by VISUAL-I T1 (PP_SPECTRAL_MATCH_001). MULTI-I does NOT re-calibrate this channel. The builder AI reads the visual effect from T1 and adds the convergence bonus from this template.

haptic_channel_effect.interpretation: Haptic contact with natural wood surfaces produces measurable parasympathetic activation via CT pathway. Effect is smaller than olfactory channel because architectural contact is intermittent.

olfactory_channel_effect.phytoncide_concentration_indoor: 20–80 μg/m³ (unfinished or lightly finished wood in ventilated rooms)
olfactory_channel_effect.cortisol_reduction: ~8% at indoor concentrations (vs. ~15% at forest concentrations of 50–200 μg/m³)
olfactory_channel_effect.nk_cell_activity_increase: ~25–30% at indoor concentrations (vs. ~52% at forest concentrations)
olfactory_channel_effect.interpretation: Indoor phytoncide exposure is approximately half the forest exposure level; physiological effects scale sublinearly.

convergence_bonus.interpretation: Multi-channel natural material exposure (visual + haptic + olfactory) produces ~20% more stress reduction than the arithmetic sum of individual channel effects. Mechanism: convergent parasympathetic activation from independent pathways.

dose_response.interpretation: Doubling wood surface area does not double stress reduction. Diminishing returns above ~40% wood surface coverage in a room. Below ~10%, phytoncide concentrations may be below threshold.

high_baseline_stress.effect: Individuals with elevated baseline cortisol show LARGER absolute stress reduction from natural materials (more room to decrease). Relative reduction is approximately constant (~8–15%).

anosmia.effect: Olfactory channel is absent; convergence bonus reduced to visual + haptic only (~10% bonus instead of 20%). Phytoncide stress reduction pathway is eliminated.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Natural material stress reduction directly serves IC2 body budget restoration: parasympathetic activation from multi-channel natural material exposure reduces allostatic load. The convergence bonus means that multi-modal natural material environments are more efficient at body budget restoration than single-channel environments (e.g., nature views alone).
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Perceived control is not a primary modulator of the natural material stress reduction pathway, which operates largely below conscious awareness (especially the olfactory channel). However, environments that provide both natural materials AND perceived control produce synergistic stress reduction via independent pathways.

natural_material_surface_fraction.interpretation: Fraction of interior surfaces that are natural materials (wood, stone, natural fibre). Optimal range: 30–50%. Below 10%: subthreshold for olfactory channel. Above 60%: diminishing returns.

wood_finish_type.interpretation: Unfinished/oiled wood releases more phytoncides than sealed/lacquered wood. Polyurethane-sealed wood releases minimal VOCs and has negligible olfactory stress reduction.

ventilation_rate.interpretation: High ventilation rates dilute indoor phytoncide concentration. Low ventilation preserves phytoncide levels but may create other IAQ issues. Optimal: moderate ventilation with natural material surfaces.

Natural material evaluation benefits from crossmodal congruence
